title: r/TalesFromTechSupport - You BLEW IT UP!!! Of Course It's Broken (Reddit Stories)
description: Honestly, this sub makes you want to bury your face in your hands... It's that bad. An ignorant manager can't put together a computer, an entitled parent refuses to follow the instructions of tech support, and yes, probably the best of all, someone literally blowing up a piece of tech. I don't even know what to say about it.   And if you like what you see then SUBSCRIBE to the channel for tons more of the best posts and stories found on Reddit.    DISCLAIMER: All stories are narrations of posts found on reddit.com and are in no way associated with either me or the channel. If you believe one of your stories has been misused then please feel free to contact me so that we can discuss the issue.

asr.full_text: Hey everybody! Welcome to another video! Welcome to r slash Tales from Tech Support! And honestly the title says it all! So let's get straight into this post by user slash Barlowcore Not too long ago, I was at a startup designing a Power meter. And I was stoked, as this was my first ever big girl job out of school. This project was my baby! My and my colleague put together skunkwork style in about a year and it could do fancy real time power reporting and analysis for grid usage and power production via SolarWind EDC. I was so damn proud of it and when we got our first big order in I was really excited for our first installs. We'd put together training days, manuals, Docs, software to configure them and thought we had it all down and ready for the big day. We designed and sold them, but the final installs were done by electricians to the company that bought them. Since they aren t engineers, we wanted it to be as simple to install as possible. All it took was 4 screws and 6 wires on the panel, all colour-coded and labelled on our device. Power it up, tell it what network to connect to, and that's all that was needed. What could go wrong, right ? Cue the very first instal! It was early Monday, I'd barely had my coffee, and a call was escalated to me. Since we were a startup, the chain was level 1, engineers who made the things. The electrician on the phone was already upset and moaning that our device wasn't working at all. So I got him to walk me through how he installed it, what happened, and what he sees. He says he wired it in just like we said, powered it up, and nothing happened, and our service did not recognise it. I got him to open it up and tried to put it into service mode. This should blinks out any errors the device sees or wiring faults. Before he can even push the button, he says the little service light on the board is just streaking out and blinking randomly. Not good. I ask him to check the colours are matching, he says it s all fine and keeps complaining that our unit is junk. Nothing more to do at this point so I tell him to rma it to me directly and will send him a new one. Now Im pretty bummed out at this point. First install, and not a single thing went right. All the checks we put in didn t help. I'm itching for this unit to come back, so when it finally does we bring it to the lab expecting some crazy firmware bug we just didn't catch. I open the lid and it just stinks of burnt electronics, right near where the power comes in there's an obvious black mark on one of the traces. Pull the board out, flip it over and our processor is just a damn crater. Follow the burnt tracers back and it goes to our sensor input. This sensor input is supposed to receive about 1 volt and this guy gave it 240. Now this sensor connector is tiny and obviously not where you power it. YET... This guy managed to force the wires into it anyways, because reading labels and matching colours is too hard! Why? JUST why?!??! On a follow-up call, the guy denied wiring it wrong or hearing any sad electronics blowing up and honestly I have no input, other than burying my face in my hands Just like the icon of this sub reddit. Our next post is brought to you by user slash KB Bradshaw Strap yourselves in for the background I'm a woman in the tech field and I just so happened to go by my last name So if you worked for the big box company but weren't in my store You probably wouldn't know my store, you probably wouldn't know my gender. This is important. Due to circumstances, we ended up getting a new manager from another store out of state. His first day was on my day off. My co-workers told me he wanted two hours with each of us to learn our thoughts on diagnosing issues and he was really eager to learn from us. He was especially interested to learn from the top tech who he heard about in his previous store. That is me, until he learned that I was a woman. I wont go into details here but his face fell when he met me for the first time. He went from wanting to meet me, and learn from me, to ignoring me or at worse, talking down to me at times! Fun! Manager got it in his head that he was going to do something to prove he knew his stuff. So when a customer came in wanting a custom built computer, which we weren't supposed to do, he grabbed the opportunity. He helped the guy pick out the parts, compare prices, and sold him the labor to put it all together. He also told me he was going to build it in the repair space, taking away a whole bench in the process from me. And he was doing this alone, and I'll never forget this. Don't tell me how to do this, let me learn! Oh I will. Cue the manager putting this machine together on the bench behind me while I continued my work just waiting. Manager has it together, hits the power switch, computer turns on, then off, then on, then off. He unplugs it then takes it apart. Then puts it together again, same result. As someone who puts together a lot of computers I know it's something to do with the processor right away based on the power cycle. Because a tech I know is good helped him install the parts I know they're in right. I also glanced at the box which has the socket of the motherboard listed as compatible. So there's really only one option left after that. So I can hear the wheels turning behind me, but he told me not to give him advice, so I keep working with my mouth shut. Let me ask him when he's good and ready. He then believes parts must be bad, so he has the customer send parts back, wait for the new ones, then try again. Same result. This continues for TWO months he has the customer who was obviously very angry at this point sent every single part back then have a whole new set of parts delivered he has promised the customer this is the last time this time it'll work he definitely knows what he's doing the day arrives where the customer brings in the room without being pushed past him and his body is not moving as much as it should. Then you might wanna stop him now. Just get over what he's done to me and just give the man the next push. But he does! Because he's not in our control. And it's just not in our control if you ask me. He hits the power, same result. He is furious. He throws the screwdriver, across the bench, denting the wall, and curses so loudly, I'm sure, a customer heard. He puts his hands, on either side of the machine, head down, shoulders slumped, utterly defeated. In a quiet, oh so quiet voice, he asks, What's wrong with me… The motherboard and processor aren't compatible without a BIOS update. How long have you known this? Since you first turned it on two months ago… He turns, he is red in the face, veins are bulging and I'm pretty sure he thought about decking me for a second before composing himself with a very very deep breath. Why didn't you say anything then?! Because you told me not to, and to let you learn. So, have you learnt? He stimmed off and out of the store. He ended up taking two personal days and I ended up building a new PC that actually worked without having to ship a new CPU just to install the update customers call once I explained everything I showed them how a cable managed to love the best cooling and looks with a clear case if it came very legendary story to tell all new tex not only as a cautionary tale always ask for help but also as a fun jab at management, who seldom understands tech. But honestly, this post is also a perfect example of malicious compliance, and who doesn't love a bit of malicious compliance… Our next post is by user slash nevernudeNR13 When I got this ticket, it had been open for six-plus months. Gone through 5-6 technicians, technicians on first second and third line and they've done pretty much everything humanly possible short of swapping out the whole computer but nothing has helped there's probably around 80 to 100 tech hours put into this so far weird thing is the error message is clearly logged and it points to a known issue. Could the other techs really have missed this? Nope, the first tech emailed the customer a link to the update that fixes the issue inside of fifteen minutes from the first call, and i see three other techs have directed the customer back to the first email with instructions to install the fix Each time, the customer has responded that she she did but it didn't cause any change in the problem. Still getting the same error message. I had a gut feeling and sent her the link to the update again. This time saying that, hey, I'm got something new for you to test. The next morning I call the customer. Hi. I emailed your link to a new patch, which should fix the problem you're having with the game, have you had a chance to try it? Yea, I did, and the games working now but this is such trashy support, entirely unacceptable to wait six months, think of my poor son who hasn't been able to play his Christmas present and goes off on a rant about how much we suck... I'm sorry to hear that, but could I ask you just one thing? See, the link I sent you is exactly the same one that we sent you on the very first day you called us. And I see in the vlog that you replied to that email saying that you had installed it, but it didn't change anything. Is that correct? The first link? No, I didn't bother with that one! Everyone knows that the first thing you suggest never works? So I just said I did. I can't believe it took you 6 months! How are you going to explain this to my son? Sorry man, looks like we sent you the solution on the very first day! But YOU chose not to follow the instructions! But as things are now working I'm going to close your ticket, and I'll leave it up to you to explain the a kid why it took so long. Honestly, how ignorant do you have to be to ignore FOUR people telling you to click on a link and still not do it, Honestly this blows my mind All right everyone! That's it for me! I hope you enjoyed this little video, and if you did make sure to subscribe for reddit videos every second day! Will see you all next time!

We'd put together training days, manuals, Docs, software to configure them and thought we had it all down and ready for the big day. We designed and sold them, but the final installs were done by electricians to the company that bought them. Since they aren t engineers, we wanted it to be as simple to install as possible. All it took was 4 screws and 6 wires on the panel, all colour-coded and labelled on our device. Power it up, tell it what network to connect to, and that's all that was needed. What could go wrong, right ? Cue the very first instal! It was early Monday, I'd barely had my coffee, and a call was escalated to me. Since we were a startup, the chain was level 1, engineers who made the things. The electrician on the phone was already upset and moaning that our device wasn't working at all. So I got him to walk me through how he installed it, what happened, and what he sees. He says he wired it in just like we said, powered it up, and

nothing happened, and our service did not recognise it. I got him to open it up and tried to put it into service mode. This should blinks out any errors the device sees or wiring faults. Before he can even push the button, he says the little service light on the board is just streaking out and blinking randomly. Not good. I ask him to check the colours are matching, he says it s all fine and keeps complaining that our unit is junk. Nothing more to do at this point so I tell him to rma it to me directly and will send him a new one. Now Im pretty bummed out at this point. First install, and not a single thing went right. All the checks we put in didn t help. I'm itching for this unit to come back, so when it finally does we bring it to the lab expecting some crazy firmware bug we just didn't catch. I open the lid and it just stinks of burnt electronics, right near where the power comes in there's an obvious black mark on one of the traces. Pull the board out, flip it over and our processor is just a damn crater. Follow the burnt tracers back and it goes to our sensor input. This sensor input is supposed to receive about 1 volt and this guy gave it 240. Now this sensor connector is tiny and obviously not where you power it. YET... This guy managed to force the wires into it anyways, because reading labels and matching colours is too hard! Why? JUST why?!??! On a follow-up call, the guy denied wiring it wrong or hearing any sad electronics blowing up and honestly I have no input, other than burying my face in my hands Just like the icon of this sub reddit.
